questions.q: What role does WSFC play in an Availability Group, per this lesson?
options: It provides cluster membership, health detection, and quorum — and its logic is what actually triggers automatic failover, not SQL Server itself
It stores the actual database files shared by all replicas
It is a SQL Server feature with no relationship to Windows Server
It only matters for FCI, never for Availability Groups
questions.explain: WSFC is a Windows Server role, not a SQL Server feature; SQL Server registers the AG as a cluster resource, and WSFC's quorum/health logic drives automatic failover.

questions.q: How do secondary replicas in an AG receive data from the primary?
options: Via log records shipped over the network — each replica has its own independent local storage
Via shared storage, the same disks the primary uses
Secondaries do not receive any data automatically
Only through nightly full backup restores
questions.explain: Unlike FCI, AG replicas do not share storage — the primary ships transaction log records over the network, and each secondary hardens them to its own copy of the database.

questions.q: What does the Availability Group listener actually do?
options: It provides a virtual network name and IP that always resolves to whichever replica is currently primary
It physically load-balances read queries across all replicas automatically
It is a monitoring dashboard for AG health only
It replaces the need for a primary replica entirely
questions.explain: The listener is a VNN/VIP abstraction — applications connect to it instead of a specific server name, and it always routes to the current primary, so failover doesn't require connection string changes.

questions.q: Why must databases in an Availability Group be in FULL recovery model?
options: Because AGs rely on shipping and replicating the transaction log itself, which requires FULL — SIMPLE truncates the log and provides nothing to ship
Because FULL recovery model is required by Windows Server Failover Clustering, unrelated to AGs
Because FULL recovery model disables all bulk operations, which AGs require
There is no such requirement — any recovery model works
questions.explain: AGs replicate via the transaction log, and only FULL recovery model retains the log history needed for that continuous log shipping to secondaries.

questions.q: A Standard Edition instance is added as a secondary replica alongside Enterprise Edition replicas in one AG. What happens to the AG's feature set, per this lesson?
options: The whole AG is constrained to Basic AG behavior — single database, no readable secondary — even on the Enterprise replicas
Nothing changes; each replica keeps its own edition's full feature set independently
The Enterprise replicas are automatically downgraded to Standard Edition licensing
The Standard Edition replica is simply ignored and excluded from the AG
questions.explain: Because the AG as a whole can't rely on features the Standard replica doesn't support, mixing editions caps the entire AG at Basic AG limitations.
